title: The Brain Acts Before the Blood Changes

scenes.tts: A water-restricted mouse starts to drink. Within a minute, a population of its thirst neurons goes quiet. Yet five minutes after water access, the salt in its blood is still raised. If the brain only corrected errors it had measured in the blood, that could not happen. So what is it responding to?
scenes.visual: Two stacked time panels: thirst-neuron activity falls within a minute of drinking, blood osmolality stays raised to five minutes; a question ends the scene.
scenes.narration: A water-restricted mouse starts to drink. Within a minute, a population of its thirst neurons goes quiet. Yet five minutes after water access, the salt in its blood is still raised. If the brain only corrected errors it had measured in the blood, that could not happen. So what is it responding to?

scenes.tts: A homeostatic loop has four parts. The regulated variable is what is held steady, here plasma osmolality. A sensor measures it: osmosensitive neurons in the lamina terminalis. A comparator decides how far it is from where it should be. An effector pushes back. Vasopressin, or A V P, saves water at the kidney. Thirst takes water in. The response opposes the error, so this is negative feedback.
scenes.visual: Four boxes in a ring joined by flow arrows; a red inhibitory arrow from effector back to the variable closes the loop.
scenes.caption: A homeostatic loop has four parts. The regulated variable is what is held steady, here plasma osmolality. A sensor measures it: osmosensitive neurons in the lamina terminalis. A comparator decides how far it is from where it should be. An effector pushes back. Vasopressin, or AVP, saves water at the kidney. Thirst takes water in. The response opposes the error, so this is negative feedback.

scenes.tts: A hormone loop has a threshold, where the response starts, and a gain, how much it grows per unit of error above threshold. For healthy adults, one summary gives a threshold of two hundred eighty four milliosmoles per kilogram. The gain is zero point four three picomoles per litre for each milliosmole per kilogram. Treat both as illustrative averages. Below threshold, the line predicts no release.
scenes.visual: Axes of vasopressin against osmolality; the threshold line, then the rising line, the equation and the hedge appear; the flat part below threshold is labelled no release.
scenes.caption: A hormone loop has a threshold, where the response starts, and a gain, how much it grows per unit of error above threshold. For healthy adults, one summary gives a threshold of 284 mOsm/kg. The gain is 0.43 pmol/L for each mOsm/kg. Treat both as illustrative averages. Below threshold, the line predicts no release.
scenes.narration: A hormone loop has a threshold, where the response starts, and a gain, how much it grows per unit of error above threshold. For healthy adults, one summary gives a threshold of 284 mOsm/kg. The gain is 0.43 pmol/L for each mOsm/kg. Treat both as illustrative averages. Below threshold, the line predicts no release.

scenes.tts: Take a hypothetical adult on that line, at steady state. Osmolality is two hundred ninety four, ten above threshold. Vasopressin is four point three zero. After drinking, osmolality is two hundred ninety, and vasopressin is two point five eight. It fell by one point seven two. Less error, less hormone. A pure feedback loop reacts to an error it has measured.
scenes.visual: Same line; a point at 294 with drop lines, then a point at 290 as osmolality moves left, then a bracket for the 1.72 fall.
scenes.caption: Take a hypothetical adult on that line, at steady state. Osmolality is 294, ten above threshold. Vasopressin is 4.30. After drinking, osmolality is 290, and vasopressin is 2.58. It fell by 1.72. Less error, less hormone. A pure feedback loop reacts to an error it has measured.

scenes.tts: In water-restricted mice, the neurons fall quiet within a minute of drinking. Seeing water without being allowed to drink does not lower their activity. In salt-challenged mice, licking an empty bottle does not either. So something that comes with drinking turns them down, ahead of any change in the blood. That is feedforward control, a response to a disturbance that is expected.
scenes.visual: Three rows of neuron activity: drinking falls, seeing water stays high, licking an empty bottle stays high; feedforward is named at the end.
scenes.narration: In water-restricted mice, the neurons fall quiet within a minute of drinking. Seeing water without being allowed to drink does not lower their activity. In salt-challenged mice, licking an empty bottle does not either. So something that comes with drinking turns them down, ahead of any change in the blood. That is feedforward control, a response to a disturbance that is expected.

scenes.tts: Researchers put water straight into the stomach. In hydrated mice, it inhibited the neurons after about one hundred five seconds, before any detectable change in blood osmolarity. Keep the limits. This is a population calcium signal in mice, not the feeling of thirst. Feedback reacts to a measured error. Feedforward acts on an expected one. Thirst uses both.
scenes.visual: Gut circuit with an inhibitory arrow to the neurons and blood unchanged; then the limits; then feedback and feedforward side by side.
